Conversions

Basement Conversion in London

A basement conversion in London turns a damp, unused cellar into dry, warm living space: a family room, home office, gym or guest bedroom. When the roof is not an option, or you have already converted the loft, the space under your house is the next place to look.

  • Existing cellars converted into habitable rooms
  • Waterproofing designed to BS 8102
  • Often no planning permission needed
  • Ventilation, insulation and escape routes included

Get a Free Basement Quote

No obligation. We call you back within one working day.

What's included

What a Basement Conversion Includes

  • Survey: head height, signs of damp, the condition of walls and floor, and the drainage position.
  • Waterproofing design to BS 8102, usually a cavity drainage membrane with a sump and pump.
  • Floor: a new insulated floor, sometimes lowered to gain head height.
  • Structural work where walls need underpinning or openings need steel beams.
  • Ventilation and daylight: mechanical ventilation and, where planning allows, a lightwell.
  • Fire safety: an escape window or protected route, and linked smoke alarms.
  • Fit-out and Building Regulations sign-off for a change to habitable use.

Is it right for you?

Signs Your Cellar Is Ready for Conversion

  • Your house has an existing cellar you can walk into, even if it is low or damp.
  • You have already converted the loft, or the roof is unsuitable.
  • You need a room away from the bedrooms: a gym, cinema room or office.
  • Your street is in a conservation area where roof extensions are refused.
  • Houses nearby have already converted their cellars.

Our process

How a Basement Conversion Is Done

  1. Free survey, including damp readings and head height.
  2. Waterproofing and structural design, plus planning and party wall checks.
  3. Strip out of old finishes, debris and any rotten timber.
  4. Floor lowering or underpinning, where needed for head height.
  5. Waterproofing: membrane, drainage channels, sump and pump.
  6. Insulation, services and fit-out.
  7. Building control sign-off as a habitable room.

Options

Basement Waterproofing Options Compared

SystemHow it worksBest for
Cavity drainage membraneA studded membrane on walls and floor lets water drain to a sump, where a pump removes itMost London cellars; tolerates movement and future water ingress
Cementitious tankingA waterproof coating bonded to the walls and floor that holds water backSound masonry with low water pressure
Combined systemTanking plus a membrane for two layers of protectionHigh water tables and bedrooms or high-value finishes

Pricing

How Much Does a Basement Conversion Cost in London?

MyBuilder puts a London cellar conversion at around £45,000 to £75,000, and Homebuilding advises allowing about £1,350 to £1,650 per square metre plus VAT for a straightforward cellar conversion.1, 2 The main factors are:

  • Head height: lowering the floor and underpinning walls adds significant cost.
  • Water: the more water present, the more robust the waterproofing system needed.
  • Lightwells: they bring in daylight and an escape route but need excavation and planning.
  • Access: removing spoil through a terraced house is slower than through a side entrance.
  • Fit-out: a shower room, kitchenette or cinema setup adds to the base cost.

Local knowledge

Basement Conversions on London Clay

Much of London sits on London Clay, which holds water and swells and shrinks with the seasons. That is why waterproofing matters more here than almost anywhere else, and why most London basements use a drained cavity membrane that copes with movement. Many Victorian houses in inner boroughs were built with coal cellars or vaults under the front path. Several inner London councils have policies limiting how far new basements can extend under gardens, so we check yours before design starts.

Why Choose Us for Your Basement Conversion

BS 8102

Waterproofing to the British Standard

BS 8102 is the code of practice for protecting below-ground structures from water. We design every basement's waterproofing to it, choosing the right grade of protection for how you will use the room, with a maintainable pump and an alarm, so a failure never goes unnoticed.

Party Wall Rules Followed

If excavation comes within 3 metres of a neighbour's building and goes below their foundations, the Party Wall etc. Act 1996 requires at least one month's notice. We identify this at the survey and help you serve the right notices, so the work starts without disputes.

Honest, Itemised Pricing

London cellar conversions typically start around £45,000. Our fixed written quote separates waterproofing, structure, services and fit-out, so you can see where the money goes and choose where to spend more or less.

How it works

Your Loft Conversion, Step by Step

FAQ

Basement Conversion FAQs

How much does a basement conversion cost in London?

MyBuilder puts a London cellar conversion at around £45,000 to £75,000, and Homebuilding advises allowing about £1,350 to £1,650 per square metre plus VAT for a straightforward cellar conversion. Digging out a new or deeper basement costs far more. You get a fixed written quote after the free survey.

Do I need planning permission to convert my cellar?

Converting an existing cellar into living space usually does not need planning permission if the outside of the house is not changed. Adding a lightwell, a new external entrance or digging deeper usually does. Listed buildings and some conservation areas have stricter rules.

How do you stop a basement being damp?

With a waterproofing system designed to British Standard BS 8102, the code of practice for protecting structures below ground from water. That is usually a cavity drainage membrane that channels any water to a sump and pump, or a cementitious tanking coating, sometimes both.

Do I need a party wall notice for a basement?

If you excavate within 3 metres of a neighbour's building to a depth below their foundations, the Party Wall etc. Act 1996 requires at least one month's notice. Work directly on a shared wall needs two months' notice.

Can a basement be used as a bedroom?

Yes, if it has a safe means of escape in a fire, such as an escape window into a lightwell or a protected route to an exit, plus adequate ventilation and daylight. Building control checks these before signing the room off as habitable.
